name: Lefty Production Co.
old_description: ONE STOP SHOP APPAREL AND ACCESSORIES DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT & PRODUCTION
about:
Lefty Production Co. operates from a suite on West 9th Street in downtown Los Angeles, California. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but its principals describe learning the trade by producing collections in Asia and South America before returning to domestic manufacturing. The team is led by Marta Miller, a former apparel brand owner, and includes pattern makers and sewers with years of industry experience.

The firm functions as a one‑stop development house and contract manufacturer for apparel and accessories. Its service chain covers sourcing and design, pattern making, sample creation, duplicate samples, marking and grading, size testing, laser cutting, cutting and sewing, and final packing. Production runs range from small batches to larger volumes, with low minimums offered to clients who complete development through Lefty. All work is performed in their Los Angeles facility.

Clients span independent designers, established fashion labels, and major retailers. The company cites collaborations with high‑fashion names such as Matthew Williamson, Rosetta Getty, and Christian Siriano, as well as retail accounts including Nordstrom and Neiman Marcus. It has also produced official uniforms for NBC’s Spartan Ultimate Team Challenge and Netflix’s Ultimate Beastmaster, bomber jackets for the Guns N’ Roses Not in This Lifetime Tour, and the prize package for the Project Runway Junior Season 2 winner. Smaller brands like Touch of Terry, Swoveralls, and Major Blue are referenced in testimonials.

Lefty emphasizes a partnership model built on transparent, flat‑rate pricing and discounts tied to the number of designs. The company highlights its commitment to Made‑in‑USA production, decades of collective experience across global supply chains, and active engagement with fashion programs at FIDM, Cal Poly, and Santa Monica College. It was recognized by the Los Angeles Business Journal in 2015.

name: Legacy Fabrics
old_description: Drafting Your Own Sloper - TWO DAY INTENSIVE - Class with Maya Jones
about:
Legacy Fabrics operates a brick-and-mortar fabric store in downtown Mission, Kansas, serving the Kansas City metropolitan area. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The store carries a rotating selection of fashion fabrics, including rayon jerseys, french terry knits, and other apparel-weight textiles sold by the yard. In addition to yardage, Legacy Fabrics stocks sewing patterns from independent designers such as Style Arc, a range of buttons and closures — including shell, horn-look, and fur-covered buttons — and notions such as needles, marking tools, and dye. The shop also hosts hands-on sewing classes, including corset-making workshops with instructor Sarah Martin and sloper-drafting intensives with Maya Jones.

Customers include home sewers, fashion students, and hobbyists seeking specialty garment fabrics and instruction not typically found in big-box retailers. The product mix emphasizes garment-making supplies rather than quilting or craft materials.

The company emphasizes an in-store experience with a larger inventory than its website displays, encouraging local visits for full selection.

name: Legacy Woodworking & Design | Las Vegas | Built-ins, Butcher Block, CNC
old_description: We design and build custom furniture and built-ins designed to transform spaces and impress your clients and guests.
about:
Legacy Woodworking & Design operates from Henderson, Nevada, where partners Ken Beck and Eric Carr lead a custom woodworking shop focused on built-in furniture and architectural millwork.

The shop offers a full-service woodworking operation that includes CNC machining, laser engraving and cutting, and traditional cabinetmaking. Services span design consultation, field measurements, 3D rendering, shop fabrication, and delivery with installation. Projects range from residential built-in offices, entertainment centers, bookcases, floating shelves, and butcher block countertops to commercial reception counters, accent walls, conference tables, and custom desks.

Clients include homeowners, interior designers, general contractors, marketing firms, exposition companies, and restaurant or bar operators seeking custom serving trays, flight holders, and presentation boards. The company also supports on-demand manufacturing for businesses needing prototypes or short production runs.

Legacy Woodworking & Design emphasizes a partner-driven approach, handling every detail from initial consultation through final installation. The team highlights its ability to combine digital fabrication with hands-on craftsmanship to deliver one-of-a-kind pieces on schedule.

name: Legacy Woodworking LLC
old_description: Legacy Woodworking, LLC is proud to offer our professional woodworking services to all of Connecticut,
about:
Legacy Woodworking LLC operates from Meriden, Connecticut, serving clients across Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, and New England. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The shop specializes in architectural millwork, custom cabinetry, and one-of-a-kind pieces that repurpose aeronautic, marine, or industrial materials. Core services include cut-to-size parts on a Holzher Cut 85 horizontal beam saw holding .0001-inch tolerance, edge banding in PVC, plastic laminate, wood veneer, and thin solid wood, and CNC machining on a Holzher Pro Master 7123 for cabinet parts, curved components, and custom fixtures. A computerized labeling system tracks parts through fabrication.

Customers span corporate, institutional, financial services, healthcare, retail, and residential sectors, with projects ranging from commercial casework and reception desks to custom trim and moldings.

Legacy emphasizes precision and versatility, offering job-shop fabrication for clients who need machined parts without investing in jigs or tooling, and highlighting its ability to transform reclaimed industrial components into distinctive furniture.

name: Legion Lighting
old_description: Energy-efficient architectural LED lighting equipment since 1946
about:
Legion Lighting, based in Deer Park, New York, has been designing and manufacturing architectural LED lighting equipment since 1946. The company is a family‑owned, third‑generation business that began as a domestic lighting producer and has operated continuously from its New York plant for nearly eight decades.

The firm produces a broad line of commercial and architectural luminaires — including healthcare fixtures, task lights, stairwell lighting, linear strips, recessed and pendant fixtures, vapor‑tight and NSF‑rated units, high‑bay lights, and agricultural lighting — all fabricated in‑house. Its facility employs CAD/CAM engineering linked to computer‑integrated manufacturing (CIM) equipment and a fully automated powder‑coat finishing system, allowing customization of shape, size, lumen output, color temperature, and dimming options.

Legion serves specifiers, electrical contractors, distributors, and end users across commercial, institutional, healthcare, agricultural, and government sectors. Its product range includes New York City‑approved exit and emergency fixtures, BABA‑compliant “Made in USA” options, and ENERGY STAR‑listed LED engines, reflecting demand from public‑works and energy‑efficiency projects.

The company attributes its longevity to a “company that cares” philosophy emphasizing personalized service, on‑time delivery, and robust build quality using high‑grade raw materials. In‑house engineering and finishing capabilities enable rapid prototyping and tailored solutions for unique architectural requirements.

name: Lenex Steel - Indianapolis | Corporate Office
old_description: Partnering with general contractors and developers nationwide to provide precision fabrication, project management, and design-build expertise to every project.
about:
Lenex Steel is headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. The company has been delivering complex structural steel projects for over two decades, serving clients across the United States.

The firm provides a full suite of structural steel services, including fabrication, value engineering, connection design, design-assist, design-build, and plan-and-spec execution. Each project is managed by a dedicated team and a single project manager from initial drawings through final delivery, eliminating handoffs and ensuring accountability. The company handles structural, heavy, complex, and miscellaneous steel packages for projects of varying scale.

Lenex Steel works primarily with general contractors, developers, architects, and engineers in the industrial and automotive sectors, among others. Its project portfolio spans operating rooms, manufacturing facilities, arena floors, and other high-profile buildings that define industries and communities nationwide.

The company emphasizes a single-point-of-responsibility model for the entire steel package, combining fabrication with design and project management to reduce risk and streamline schedules. This integrated approach, rooted in decades of Midwest expertise, is designed to overcome obstacles before construction begins and to deliver structures on schedule and to specification.

about:
LexPlastics, Inc. operates from Lexington, Kentucky, with easy access to interstate highways and major truck lines. The company has over 39 years of experience in the plastics industry, building a reputation for custom injection molding and tooling design.

The company specializes in custom injection molding using both horizontal and vertical presses, with 22 machines ranging from 35 to 500 tons of clamping force. It applies scientific molding principles to produce high-volume, close-tolerance precision parts from engineering-grade to commodity resins. LexPlastics also designs and builds complete production tooling in-house, including extrusion dies, and offers program management, Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), and control plan initiatives.

LexPlastics serves the plastics industry broadly, working with customers who require precision molded components and tooling. Its project management team, with over 160 years of combined experience, supports customers from concept through product launch.

The company emphasizes a philosophy of "Doing the Right Thing for Everyone," focusing on proactive maintenance, comprehensive resin review, and engineering product launch effectiveness to ensure on-time and accurate delivery.

about:
Liberty Auto Parts operates from a facility at 150‑ in the Jamaica neighborhood of Queens, New York. The business is family owned and operated, though the founding year and original founders are not publicly disclosed.

The shop stocks new and used auto parts for all makes and models and provides on‑site installation through its full‑service automotive repair shop. It also offers a range of service plans and backs every part purchased and installed on the premises with an extended warranty. A nationwide parts locating system helps source hard‑to‑find components, and all parts undergo rigorous testing before sale. The company accepts major credit cards including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover.

In addition to walk‑in consumers, the company serves small businesses including franchised dealerships and independent repair garages.

Liberty Auto Parts positions itself as a state‑of‑the‑art one‑stop shop, distinguishing itself through its extended warranty on installed parts, its nationwide locating network, and its testing protocol.
